see.pr: US$15 basic admissions (2022), more to swim with dolphins and other activities
see.b: In the middle of the La Isla Shopping Village in the hotel zone, this small, modern aquarium lets you get up close and personal with aquatic life. You can pet rays, nurse sharks, touch starfish, etc. You can pay to swim with captive…

Small Maya archaeological site on the south end of the hotel zone. The settlement was at its peak around 250-600 AD. There are 47 structures here as well as a small site museum. Bring mosquito repellant.

see.n: Museo Maya de Cancún and Archaeological Zone of San Miguelito
see.b: Museum about the Maya civilization and its many sites in the Yucatan Peninsula. Large number of artifacts from sites in and around Cancun. Next door is the San Miguelito ruins, which are partially restored and include a small pyramid.

see.a: Blvd. Kukulcan 12.5, El Rey, Zona Hotelera
see.pr: Free (but may take effort to ignore touts from Westin)
see.b: Ruins of a small Maya temple on the grounds of the Westin.

see.a: Blvd. Kukulcan Km. 9, Punta Cancun, Zona Hotelera
see.b: Classic red and white striped tubular lighthouse on the northern tip of the Hotel Zone.

Ruins of a Maya port from about 600 AD. El Castillo is the largest structure at the site, it is a five-level pyramid with a height of 12.5 meters and a temple at the top. A small site museum is available.

see.n: Torre Escénica del Embarcadero de Cancún
see.a: Blvd. Kukulcan Km. 4.5, Kukulcan Boulevard, Zona Hotelera
see.pr: Included with cost of Xcaret ferry (show bracelet)
see.b: 80-m tower with a rotating observation deck that takes about 30 minutes for a full revolution.

see.a: Supermanzana 053 Manzana 1 L 1-01 Av. KABAH, Av. Nichupté
see.b: Urban ecological park with lush junglescapes and roaming wildlife including lots of friendly coatis who will gladly take that leftover burger and fries off your hands. Lots of birds, iguanas and turtles. Playgrounds for kids. Exercise…
Modern 2-story public building in a broad pedestrian square with fountains, night lights & tall trees.

see.a: Blvd. Kukulcan, La Isla, Zona Hotelera
see.b: Tourist trap wax museum that charges too much for admission then has the audacity to tell visitors they can't take pictures.

see.n: Museo del Automóvil Antiguo del Sureste
see.a: Av. Puerto Juárez entre Calle 89, Mza 116, Lote 14 16
see.b: Private automobile collection with lots of well-restored muscle cars.

see.a: Blvd. Kukulcan km 12.5, La Isla, Zona Hotelera
see.b: 3 turns in an air-conditioned gondola.
Shows and dinner on a pirate boat.
A theme park, which is built around the culture of Mexico, food, music and customs in the Mayan jungle. It's on the highway, so easily accessible with a second-class bus or colectivos.
Take a trip out on the calm lagoon on a beautiful boat. Steak and lobster is cooked on the boat. Romantic twilight and midnight cruises available.
Yacht rentals for exploring all areas of Cancún, snorkeling, diving, swimming the other water activities in your own private yacht. Powerboats, catamarans, and mega yachts available.
Drive your own boat through the lagoon in the Jungle Tour and snorkel on the reef. Diving lessons and dive trips to popular dive spots in Cancún such as underwater museum.
Exciting water tour. Choose either a jet ski or two person jet boat for a trip through the lagoon out to snorkel on the reef. Popular tours are the Jungle Tour and the Sailing Quest (Catamarans).
Off-road ATV adventures. Also offers horseback riding, zip lining, and cenote swimming.
Private and shared deep-sea fishing trips from Cancun and Isla Mujeres. Includes gear, drinks, licenses, and professional crew.

see.a: Blvd. Kukulcan Km. 5.8, Kukulcan Boulevard, Zona Hotelera
see.b: Charter fishing trips starting at US$680 for 4 hours, including bait, tackle, snacks, drinks.

see.a: Blvd. Kukulkan 6 (km 6 of Cancun Hotel Zone)
see.b: Shared deep-sea fishing trips (6 hours). Join other travelers and share the cost of the boat. Includes beers, soft drinks, ice, bait, fishing licenses, and professional crew. The dock fee of US$15 per person is not included.
An alternative to spending the day bouncing across waves on a deep-water boat, this outfit specializes in shallow water fishing with fly fishing and light tackle fishing trips.

18-hole jungle course that's well maintained and one of the least expensive golf courses in the region. Rental equipment and carts are a bit worn and about due for an upgrade, but for most visitors, this is one of the best options since…
Modern seaside 18-hole jungle course designed by Jack Nicklaus. Holes 14 and 15 are played next to the ocean. Putting green, club house and other amenities on-site.

Resort course that's a bit older, but well maintained, though the rental clubs and carts show their age. The clubhouse serves a nice breakfast if you're getting an early start. There are a couple of crocodiles living along the course,…

see.a: Av. Bonampak Lote 10, int. 1 Smza.2, Puerto Acapulco S/N, Zona Hotelera
see.b: Well kept course with a number of water and sand traps. Holes 13 and 14 are adjacent to the ocean and usually have quite a bit of wind to mess with your shots. The best time to golf is early morning when temperatures are still cool, but…

see.a: Prol. Bonampak, Carr. a Punta Sam s/n
see.b: Resort golf course with beautiful fairways but some rough conditions on the greens. Course is designed by Greg Norman and has some very difficult holes. Expect to lose lots of balls if you slice into the rough, which is mostly swamp.…
Natural golf course that's not well manicured with older rental equipment.
Jack Nicklaus Signature golf course with 27 holes featuring jungle and beach settings. Drinks available every 2-3 holes. Manicured fairways and greens.

Wet'n'Wild also offers dolphin experiences. (Beware: no cameras are allowed, they charge for the first photo and a bit less for each subsequent one). Other great places to swim with captive dolphins are Delphinus Dreams and Dolphin…
Scuba dive with a wide catalog of diving programs.
Professional PADI certified scuba diving company provides PADI Diving certifications.

see.a: Blvd. Kukulcan KM 3.5, Kukulcan Boulevard, Zona Hotelera
see.pr: Half-day dive trips start at US$69
see.b: PADI certified scuba instructors. Equipment rentals. Day trips to reefs, sunken ships, and cave diving (cenotes).

PADI certified dive instructors offering a variety of courses including Advanced Open Water and Divemaster as well as day trips to popular dive sites along the Great Mesoamerican Reef, Isla Mujeres, Cozumel, Cenotes and underwater…
PADI and SDI diving instruction. Reef trips, cenote trips, dive trips to Undersea Museum (MUSE).
Full service dive shop. PADI certified instructors and courses. Trips to MUSA (undersea museum), reefs, etc. Cenote diving available. Equipment included.
A family-owned scuba diving center operating since the early 2000s. PADI-certified instructors lead small groups (maximum 4 divers).

see.a: Av. Rodrigue Gomez y Av. Mayapan
see.b: Since 2020, Cancún Fútbol Club, a team in the Expansion League has played professional soccer in this small, 18,800-seat stadium in downtown. The stadium is seldom crowded.

The stadium was named after former MLB and LMB player Beto Avila (known as Bobby Avila in Cleveland, where he played 10 seasons for the Indians). Cancun has had several professional baseball teams over the years, first the Marlins, then…

eat.b: There is a good variety. The eateries are open from 10:00 and the food stalls from the evening on. All of them close around 00:00. Most places have a big sign showing the food on a picture and the according low price. Tacos as low as 30…

eat.n: Food stall directly in front of the bus station
eat.b: They have tasty tortas (sandwich) for M$25 and tacos.
Here you get well tasting tacos with fish (e.g. shrimps) for M$25 or with meat.
Their red pozole and tamales is very tasty. Excellent Guerrero style food. The restaurant looks quite old which is also it’s charme.
Very good taqueria. Authentic Mexican food. Great portion. The waiters are very friendly. Nice atmosphere.
Very good buffet. The food with a homemade touch. Variety of dishes. The attention is very good.
There is a Comida Corrida including a soup, main dish, tortillas and drink for M$60-70. They also serves breakfast starting at M$50.
You get a Chinese dish for M$65-80.
As the name says, here you get quesadillas for M$18 and sopes for M$21.
Serving tortas, a kind of Mexican sandwich.
An extremely good sampling of Mexican food from all around the country. Excellent value. Nothing fancy but a gastronomical delight. Try the "Huevos Motuleños".
Taco restaurant specializing in seafood. Fish tacos cost M$37 (July 2021) and are a few pieces of fried fish with some tortillas. You put your own sauces and condiments.
Really nice and laid back seafood restaurant where everything's deep fried. Try the chiles rellenos, possibly the best ones in Cancún.

La Habichuela is a must-visit with its Mexican cuisine, Mayan setting and Caribbean seafood. This restaurant has been open since 1977 and is a legend in Cancún. The romantic, outside garden is a popular place to dine with the decoration…
Art exhibitions every 15 days. Good baguettes and wine.
Classic Mexican taqueria specializing in tacos al pastor. Very popular with the locals, quite tasty and at a fair price.

Elegant restaurant serving grilled steaks and seafood along with creative deserts and an extensive wine list with notable wines from around the world, including some of the excellent wines from Mexico's Valle de Guadalupe. Better than…

This Argentine steakhouse serves up one of the best menus in Cancún. The atmosphere inside the restaurant makes you feel you have travelled an extra . The staff's attention to detail and desire to please make you feel like you're the…

eat.a: Km 10.5, Blvd. Kukulcan, Punta Cancun, Zona Hotelera

eat.b: Latin American cuisine.

eat.a: Blvd. Kukulcán, Retorno Chac L-41, Zona Hotelera
eat.b: Japanese and Thai cuisine featuring teppanyaki tables.

eat.a: Blvd Kukulcán, Retorno Chac L-41, Zona Hotelera
eat.b: Stepped up bar food with all the games on over 40 screens.

eat.a: Blvd Kukulcán, km 14.5, Lote 40-A, Zona Hotelera
eat.b: Gustino has authentic Italian cuisine using the freshest Mediterranean ingredients.

Señor Frog's is a restaurant by day and a dance club by night, and is one of the most popular spots for vacationers to visit. The restaurant opens up for lunch and serves international types of food such as pasta, chicken and pizza as…

Dady'O has been known to host some of the world's top DJs, including Red Foo (LMFAO), Apl.De.App and Tiësto, features a casual atmosphere, laser shows, pole dancing go go girls and flashing dance floor opening shows.

A nightclub featuring a show that has been compared with Las Vegas. More than 50 professionals in scenery. Tickets can be bought online for US$75. If you don't mind waiting to get in exchangeable tickets can be bought from Oxxo for M$1000.
Loud, open front party bar in the heart of the Hotel Zone. You can't miss the cow print decor or the booming bass of the non-stop party. Known for innovative drinks and a lively crowd.

eat.a: Kukulkan Km. 9.5, Punta Cancun, Zona Hotelera
eat.b: Liter-size margaritas, buckets of beer, and spicy micheladas. The house favorite is the Coco Loco, coconut juice and rum served in a coconut shell. Food options include shrimp tacos and coconut shrimp.
Lively nightclub playing a mix of music (but with far too much reggaeton). Great drinks and an option for unlimited alcohol. Wet T-shirt contests.

Try the live music bar Los 4 Elementos. They open and play live music from 23:00 until the last customer leaves. The music is great and prices are significantly lower than those found in the hotel zone clubs.
Lively club serving beer in buckets (cubetas) with casual food like wings, fries and burgers. Live music with a lot of rock and metal bands played at loud volumes. Fun place.

eat.a: Av Tulum Smz 22 Mz 5 Lote 33, Centro
eat.b: Lively atmosphere, drag performers, live music and DJs, plus great mixed drinks.
Fun atmosphere, drag queen cabaret with live music or DJs, beers and large mixed drinks.

Super small craft brewery with a range of ales from a light golden ale, a Belgian strong, a brown ale flavored with chilis, and of course, the always ubiquitous IPA. Light food includes seafood, tacos and a nice charcuterie board with…
